'''David Gareth Jones''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|CNZM}} (born 28 August 1940) is a New Zealand academic, and is an emeritus professor at the [[University of Otago]], specialising in [[neuroscience]], [[bioethics]] and [[Anatomy|anatomical education]]. He has published a number of books, including a textbook on medical ethics, and several books on medicine and [[theology]]. In 2004 Jones was appointed a Companion of the [[New Zealand Order of Merit]] for services to science and education.

==Early life and education==

Jones has a [[Bachelor of Science|Bachelor of Science with Honours]] and a [[Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery]], both from [[University College London]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |title=Advisory Committee on Assisted Reproductive Technology: Annual report 2011/12 |date=October 2012 |publisher=Advisory Committee on Assisted Reproductive Technology |location=Wellington |pages=15}}</ref> He also holds a [[Doctor of Science]] degree from the [[University of Western Australia]], and an [[Doctor of Medicine|MD]] from the University of Otago.<ref name=":0" />

==Academic career==

Jones taught and studied at the University of Western Australia before joining the faculty of the University of Otago in 1983, as head of the Department of Anatomy and Structural Biology.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |url=https://www.otago.ac.nz/about/official_documents/calendar |title=University Calendar |publisher=[[University of Otago]] |year=2005 |location=Dunedin |access-date=3 Oct 2025}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news |date=6 June 2004 |title=CNZM for services to science and education |work=[[Otago Daily Times]]}}</ref> He served four consecutive five-year terms in the role, ending in 2003.<ref name=":2" /> During his tenure he broadened the focus of the department from medical and dental students to include a greater proportion of science students, and strengthened the biomedical research focus of the department.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=McKinlay |first=Tom |date=31 Aug 2004 |title=Neuroscientist takes deputy vice-chancellor job |work=[[Otago Daily Times]]}}</ref> Jones served as Deputy Vice Chancellor (Academic and International) for five years from the beginning of 2005, and was succeeded by Professor Vernon Squires.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> In 2008 he chaired the university's gender equity working party, which recommended the appointment of a gender equity leader.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rudd |first=Alison |date=12 Dec 2009 |title=New university post; Gender equity role to be offered to female senior academic |url= |work=[[Otago Daily Times]] |via=Factiva}}</ref>

Jones was Professor of Anatomy and Structural Biology.<ref name=":0" /> He was Director of the University of Otago Bioethics Centre.<ref name=":3" /> Jones specialises in neuroscience, bioethics and anatomical education, including topics such as stem cell research, genetic testing, the use of body parts in medical education, and abortion.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Nicola |date=2023-08-13 |title=Prof. Gareth Jones – New Zealand Christians In Science (NZCIS) |url=https://www.nzcis.org/who-we-are/prof-gareth-jones/ |access-date=2025-09-08 |website=www.nzcis.org |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=University of Otago |first= |date=2023-08-01 |title=Profile: Emeritus Professor Gareth Jones |url=https://www.otago.ac.nz/anatomy/people/staff/profile?id=630 |access-date=2025-09-08 |website=www.otago.ac.nz |language=en}}</ref> He describes his research as "try[ing] to bridge the gap between science, research and policy issues."<ref name=":2" /> With two other Otago academics, Grant Gillett and [[Alastair Campbell (bioethicist)|Alastair Campbell]], Jones wrote a widely-used textbook on medical ethics, which ran to four editions.<ref name=":2" /> Jones has also written on the relationship between science and faith. After his book ''Brave New People: Ethical issues at the commencement of life'' was published in 1984 there was considerable controversy, leading Jones to explore Christian approaches to dealing with controversial issues.<ref name=":4" />

Jones was appointed emeritus professor at the University of Otago in 2012.<ref>{{Cite book |title=University Calendar |publisher=[[University of Otago]] |year=2015 |location=Dunedin}}</ref> He writes often for the ''[[Otago Daily Times]]'' on ethical and university issues.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bioethics confronting but informs debates|url=https://www.odt.co.nz/opinion/bioethics-confronting-informs-debates|website=Otago Daily Times Online News|date=2013-03-22|access-date=2025-12-01|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Academics enrich community|url=https://www.odt.co.nz/opinion/academics-enrich-community|website=Otago Daily Times Online News|date=2016-01-14|access-date=2025-12-01|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=The university challenges heading our way|url=https://www.odt.co.nz/opinion/university-challenges-heading-our-way|website=Otago Daily Times Online News|date=2024-01-22|access-date=2025-12-01|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Managers making our university tick|url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/campus/university-of-otago/managers-making-our-university-tick|website=Otago Daily Times Online News|date=2011-12-05|access-date=2025-12-01|language=en}}</ref>

One of Jones's notable doctoral students is [[Hallie Buckley]].<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Buckley |first=Hallie |title=Health and disease in the prehistoric Pacific Islands |type=Doctoral thesis |publisher=OUR Archive, University of Otago |url=https://ourarchive.otago.ac.nz/handle/10523/6804 |year=2001 |hdl=10523/6804}}</ref>

== Recognition ==
In the [[2004 Birthday Honours (New Zealand)|2004 Queen's Birthday Honours]], Jones was appointed a Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit for services to science and education.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2020-02-20 |title=Prof. Gareth Jones |url=https://www.faraday.cam.ac.uk/about/people/prof-gareth-jones/ |access-date=2025-09-08 |website=Faraday |language=EN}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=7 June 2004 |title=Queen's Birthday honours list 2004 |url=https://dpmc.govt.nz/publications/queens-birthday-honours-list-2004 |access-date=30 May 2020 |publisher=Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet}}</ref>
